title: Segmented activation stitching and buffer deflation to reduce GPU peak workspace
author: Aditi Rao
description: Summary: Introduces a segmented activation materialization strategy ("segmented activation stitching") combined with opportunistic scratch buffer deflation and a memory-aware microbatch scheduler to lower peak GPU workspace for long-sequence generation workloads. Motivation: large sequence generation and dense KV-cache workloads expose temporary allocation spikes from full-layer re-materialization and transient scratch buffers. Rather than a full-layer checkpoint/restore, this PR divides activations into smaller immutable segments that are stored in a compact delta representation and stitched on demand, enabling finer-grained eviction and smaller transient buffers. Key changes: (1) segmented activation store and stitcher for re-materialization paths; (2) a deflation routine for scratch buffers that compacts and coalesces empty slots during idle windows; (3) microbatch scheduler changes that tag batches with a memory-envelope and stagger allocations to avoid concurrent peak alignment; (4) lightweight KV-window hints that bias eviction for seldom-accessed KV windows during high pressure; (5) telemetry and smoke tests for end-to-end regression on 2x and 8x GPU configs. Compatibility: keeps the public serving API unchanged and includes a runtime flag to opt into the segmented stitcher for canary rollout. Performance summary: on internal GPT-style 8k benchmarks we observe a median 28% reduction in observed peak GPU memory and a 38% reduction in transient workspace allocations for steady-state continuous-batching workloads, with a P95 latency increase of ~2ms for worst-case re-materialization paths. Risk and mitigation: materialization-on-demand can add a small CPU/GPU recompose cost; mitigations include a per-request cold-window prefetch policy and a conservative default canary rollout. Related work: complements recent allocator tuning changes (ENG-61642, ENG-70188) and is orthogonal to quantized kernel work. Testing: unit tests for segment serialization, integration stress tests on multi-concurrency workloads, and a replay harness that validated no correctness regressions across sampled prompts. The description below lists commits, changed areas, review conversation, CI history, and the merge outcome.
commits: a1f4d3c: introduce segmented activation store and stitcher (initial design, serialization format)
b2e7f91: implement scratch buffer deflation and opportunistic coalescer; add microbatch memory-envelope tags
c9d2b5e: add KV-window hinting, telemetry metrics, tests and canary flag; address review comments
snippet_examples:
// stitcher: reconstruct segment chain into activation slice
for (auto &seg : segments) stitch_into(frame, seg.data());

// deflater: compact free slots during idle windows
if (idle_window > kDeflateThreshold) deflateScratchPool();
reviews: Liam Chen (reviewer): Overall this direction looks promising. Please add more comments around the segment on-disk format and justify the lock-free access pattern. Also run the multi-GPU stress harness with small microbatches to ensure no contention spike.

Aditi Rao (author): Addressed in commit c9d2b5e — added format docs, unit tests, and a lock-free fastpath guarded by a coarse-grained fallback. Added multi-GPU stress scenario to replay harness configs.
Marco Santini (reviewer): Observed a small P95 latency bump in the initial run, but acceptable given memory win. Request adding an opt-out flag per-serving-route for latency-sensitive apps.
Aditi Rao (author): Added route-level flag (pkg/config/runtime_flags.go) and documented trade-offs in docs/ops/memory_tuning.md.
Elena Park (approver): Verified telemetry and test coverage, CI green on second run. Approving for merge after a short canary window.

benchmark_results: 8k-seq continuous-batching (4xA100 logical): peak GPU memory -28% (baseline 62GB -> 44.6GB), transient workspace -38%
2k-seq typical traffic: peak GPU memory -12%, median latency unchanged, P95 +2ms worst-case
KV-heavy trace (200k unique keys): reduced eviction churn and 9% lower net allocations due to window hints
notes_on_deploy: Introduces runtime flag runtime.segmented_stitcher_enabled (default=false) for safe canary rollout
Recommend enabling on a small percentage of traffic and monitoring mem_metrics.segment_stitch_recomposes and mem_metrics/peak_workspace
Ops playbook updated at docs/ops/memory_tuning.md with rollback steps
release_notes: Added segmented activation stitching and scratch buffer deflation to reduce peak GPU workspace for long-sequence workloads. Opt-in via runtime.segmented_stitcher_enabled. See docs/ops/memory_tuning.md for tuning guidance.
